page: UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-2GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features a single shared AMD EPYC 9575F processor core built on the x86_64 architecture, running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of RAM and a 25 GB local SSD. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities due to the single-vCPU limitation. Single-core CPU performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 compression/decompression rates ranking in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core stress-ng performance, PassMark CPU scores, and PassMark database operations fall into the weak category (bottom 25%). Memory performance is also constrained, with read-only memory bandwidth categorized as weak and PassMark memory scores ranking in the poor tier (bottom 10%).

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity, which limits its utility for multi-threaded or memory-intensive applications. While it achieves average performance in small-scale LLM inference (135M model) and large-block memory writes, it is poorly suited for database operations or high-throughput static web serving. This configuration is best utilized for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic utility scripting, development environments, or low-traffic web applications where single-core burst performance is beneficial but overall resource demands remain minimal.
